:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider a spherical balloon with radius $r.$ As the balloon loses air, its volume $V$ decreases. What is the best interpretation of $V'(r)?$

![](images/7f/7f52288ca4670375413ecd5283bc2d15fbb332af311ead07986c1526d25e338a.png)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The function $V(r)$ gives the volume of a sphere with radius $r.$ So

$$
V'(r) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}V}{\textrm{d}r} = \dfrac{\textrm{Change in }V}{\textrm{Change in }r}.
$$

Therefore, $V'(r)$ is the rate at which the volume changes as the radius changes.

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Consider a rectangle such that the height is fixed but its base $b$ can vary. What is the best interpretation of ${A}^{′}(b)$ if $A$ is the area of the rectangle?
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The function $A(b)$ gives the area of a rectangle with base $b.$ So

$$
{A}^{′}(b)=\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}b}=\frac{\text{Change in }A}{\text{Change in }b}.
$$

Therefore, ${A}^{′}(b)$ is the rate at which the area changes as the base changes.
